111: Section 337 scope: whether goods imported by an importer and used post-importation to directly infringe a method claim at the seller's inducement are 'articles that infringe' under 19 U.S.C. 1337(a)(1)(B)(i); en banc court upheld the Commission's reasonable interpretation under Chevron, reversing the panel's contrary holding.

We hold that the Commission's interpretation that the phrase 'articles that infringe' covers goods that were used by an importer to directly infringe post-importation as a result of the seller's inducement is reasonable.
205: Domestic industry under §337(a)(3)(C): the Commission held LSI failed to prove a domestic industry relating to articles protected by the '958 patent (licensing activity not tied to patent-covered articles). Court also rejected LSI's retroactivity challenge to applying InterDigital II's standard.

We affirm the Commission's no-violation decision regarding the '958 patent. We do so on the ground that LSI has shown no error in the Commission's finding that LSI failed to establish the existence of the required domestic industry.
3276: Domestic industry under §337(a)(3)(A)-(B): whether qualitative factors alone can show significant investment in plant and equipment and significant employment of labor or capital.

We hold that qualitative factors alone are insufficient to show "significant investment in plant and equipment" and "significant employment of labor or capital" under prongs (A) and (B) of the § 337 domestic industry requirements.
5362: Economic prong of the domestic industry requirement for the '631 patent based on past R&D investment with ongoing field service nexus; found satisfied
We affirm the ITC's determination that a domestic industry exists for the '631 patent.
5800: Section 337 requirement that imported articles infringe after importation (articles that infringe, post-importation inducement)
The Commission correctly held that Section 337 applies to articles that infringe after importation.
5801: Section 337 importation requirement: whether Comcast is an importer of the X1 set-top boxes
The Commission's findings of importation by or for Comcast of articles for infringing use are supported by substantial evidence.
9045: ITC domestic industry economic prong under 19 U.S.C. 1337(a)(3)(C): Universal's substantial investment in QuickSet R&D and engineering satisfied the requirement.
Accordingly, we affirm the Commission's determination that Universal has satisfied the economic prong of the domestic industry requirement in subparagraph (a)(3)(C) of Section 337.
9148: Domestic industry technical prong under Section 337: Broadcom failed to identify an actual article practicing claim 25 of the '583 patent, so the technical prong was not met.
We agree with the Commission that Broadcom failed to satisfy the technical requirement.
10259: Domestic industry technical prong for the '439 patent; the court affirmed the Commission's finding of no domestic industry because it fell with the noninfringement finding
because the parties agree that the domestic industry findings fall with the noninfringement findings, Appellant's Reply Br. 35, we affirm the Commission on finding no domestic industry.
10528: Whether the economic prong of domestic industry is met for Reynolds products that lacked FDA premarket authorization at the time the complaint was filed.
Nothing in the plain language of the statute requires that the protected articles have regulatory approval.
10878: Domestic industry technical prong for the '530 patent: 10X's domestic products practice claim 1.
We see no reversible error in the Commission's determination.
11975: Domestic industry economic prong under section 337(a)(3): Zircon failed to show significant or substantial investments with respect to articles protected by each asserted patent because it aggregated investments across products practicing different patents; the chip R&D investment was also not shown to be substantial.
We agree and conclude that substantial evidence supports the Commission's finding that Zircon failed to meet that threshold.
12076: Domestic industry technical prong: the court held substantial evidence supports the Commission's finding that Centripetal's CleanINTERNET DI Product did not practice claim 22 limitations (b)-(f), so the technical prong was not met.
we hold that substantial evidence supports the Commission's finding that Centripetal's DI Product failed to satisfy the technical prong of the domestic industry requirement.
12163: Domestic industry economic prong under section 337(a)(3)(B): the Commission's interpretation that sales, marketing, warehousing, quality control and distribution labor or capital does not count was held legally incorrect; vacated and remanded for redetermination for the design patents.
For the foregoing reasons, we conclude that the Commission's interpretation of section 337(a)(3)(B) is incorrect.
12164: Domestic industry technical prong for the '984 utility patent: Lashify's products do not satisfy the technical prong, so the requirement was not met as to that patent.

We therefore reject Lashify's challenge to the Commission's claim construction. It follows that we must also affirm the Commission's determination that Lashify did not satisfy the technical prong of the domestic-industry requirement as to the '984 patent.
12431: Domestic industry technical and economic prongs under Section 337 were satisfied by Masimo's Masimo Watch prototypes and related investments.
Thus, we affirm the Commission’s determination that Masimo met its burden to prove that its Masimo Watch satisfies the technical prong of the domestic industry requirement of § 337.
12759: Domestic industry economic prong (19 U.S.C. §1337(a)(3)): Commission found Ventria's Optibumin investments in plant and equipment, labor, and R&D significant and substantial; affirmed.
Under these circumstances, there is substantial evidence for the Commission's finding that the domestic industry requirement is satisfied.
13183: Technical domestic industry: Bissell's domestic industry products satisfy the disabled battery charging circuit limitation, based on expert testimony relying on source code not admitted as an exhibit.
we hold that substantial evidence supports the Commission's finding that the claim limitation is met by the domestic industry products.
14900: Domestic industry technical prong for claims 18-22: domestic products found not to practice the claims, so the requirement was not met.

Dometic's only challenge to the Commission's determinations of infringement and the absence of domestic industry regarding claim 18 and dependent claims 19-22 is a challenge to Commission's construction of the 'first axis' limitation of claim 18.
